questions.question: Which of the following is considered the strongest and most secure password?
questions.hint: Look for a combination of uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and special characters.

questions.question: What is the safest action to take when you receive an unexpected email asking you to click a link to verify your account details?
options: Click the link immediately to fix the account
Reply to the email asking who sent it
Delete the email or report it as phishing
Forward the email to all your contacts
questions.hint: Legitimate companies will rarely ask for sensitive info via an unexpected link in an email.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of enabling Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) on your accounts?
options: To make the login process faster
To add a second layer of security beyond just a password
To encrypt all the files on your hard drive
To hide your browsing history from your internet provider
questions.hint: It requires two different forms of identification to prove who you are.

questions.question: Why is it generally discouraged to access sensitive information, like online banking, using public Wi-Fi?
options: Public Wi-Fi is always slower than home Wi-Fi
Public Wi-Fi uses a different version of the internet
Unencrypted public networks can allow attackers to intercept your data
Banking apps do not work on public Wi-Fi networks
questions.hint: Open networks often lack encryption, making the data traveling through them visible to others.

questions.question: Under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), what does the 'Right to Erasure' specifically allow individuals to do?
options: Delete their entire browsing history from their local computer
Request that an organization delete their personal data under certain conditions
Permanently block a specific website from accessing the internet
Force a company to stop charging them for a subscription
questions.hint: This is often referred to as the 'Right to be Forgotten'.
